title: Relaxing Parts of Your Body
summary: Relax one part at a time: forehead, temples, chin, jaw, shoulders.
script:
Hi, and welcome back. Today, we’re going to relax a few parts of your body, one part at a time.
Place your hands on your head and take a deep breath in. Feel your head under your hands.
As you breathe out, move your hands down a little, just above your eyes. This is your forehead. Forehead.
Place your fingers on your forehead and take another slow breath in. As you breathe out, let your forehead relax. Let the skin become soft. You can close your eyes if you like.
Now move your fingers to the sides of your forehead, between your eyes and your ears. These are your temples. Temples.
Place your fingers on your temples and slowly move them in small circles. Breathe in slowly… and breathe out. Keep making small circles and feel your temples relax.
Now move your hands down your face, past your eyes, your nose, and your mouth. Stop just below your mouth. This is your chin. Chin. Touch your chin and notice how it feels.
Now move your fingers from your chin to the sides of your face. This is your jaw. Jaw.
Place your fingers on your jaw. Sometimes, when we feel stressed, our jaw becomes tight without us noticing.
Take a slow breath in… and breathe out.
Let your jaw relax. Let your mouth open a little. Feeling the tension slowly go away.
Take another slow breath in… and as you breathe out, let your jaw become soft and relaxed.
Now move both hands out to the top of your body, where your arms begin. These are your shoulders. Shoulders.
We also carry a lot of tension in our shoulders. Take a deep breath in… and as you breathe out, let your shoulders drop.
Stay here for a moment and notice all these parts of your body together.
Relax your forehead.
Relax your temples.
Let your jaw become soft.
Let your shoulders drop.
Take one more slow breath in…
and breathe out.
Notice how these parts of your body feel now. Maybe they feel a little softer. Maybe a little lighter.
Just stay here for a moment and enjoy this feeling.
You learned more words than usual today, but don’t worry about remembering them all. We’ll use these words again in other meditations, especially the most important ones.
That’s why it’s important to make these meditations a habit. The more you practice, the more you’ll hear the same words again. Little by little, you’ll start to remember them naturally, without trying too hard.
For example, “drop your shoulders.” You’ll hear this phrase many times in our meditations. With time, these words and phrases will start to stay in your mind. There’s no rush.
Now, let’s go back to your forehead. Place your whole hand on your forehead and repeat:
“I can relax my forehead when I need to.”
Notice how your body feels now.
Your forehead, your temples, your jaw, and your shoulders.
You don’t need to remember every word right away. Your body is already starting to connect these words with the places you’ve touched.
Take one last slow breath in… and breathe out.
When you’re ready, slowly open your eyes. Carry this relaxed feeling with you as you continue your day.
And remember, there’s no rush. One breath, one word, and one meditation at a time.

vocabulary.definition: the part of your face just above your eyes
the sides of your forehead, between your eyes and your ears
the part of your face just below your mouth
the sides of your face below your mouth
the top of your body, where your arms begin

exercises.sentence: Which part of your face is your forehead?
options: The part just below your mouth
On the sides of your forehead, between your eyes and ears
exercises.correctAnswer: On the sides of your forehead, between your eyes and ears

exercises.sentence: Which sentence correctly describes your chin and jaw?
options: Your chin is above your eyes, and your jaw is between your eyes and ears.
Your chin is where your arms begin, and your jaw is above your eyes.
Your chin is just below your mouth, and your jaw extends along the lower sides of your face.
exercises.correctAnswer: Your chin is just below your mouth, and your jaw extends along the lower sides of your face.

exercises.sentence: In this meditation, what does “drop your shoulders” mean?
options: Lift your shoulders toward your ears
Let your shoulders move down and relax
Move your hands to your forehead
exercises.correctAnswer: Let your shoulders move down and relax
